source.title: [Interim research report] Activation plateaus & sensitive directions in GPT2

record.tranche_reason: The report discusses superposition as motivation and tests activation-perturbation predictions attributed to error correction. It does not test the listed versions’ claims about feature overlap, capacity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The report measures activation plateaus and sensitivity to directions as proposed consequences of error correction; those findings do not establish the listed versions. The KL threshold of 0.5 is used to define a sensitivity measure, not reported as an outcome value. Results from Gurnee (2024) and Lindsey (2024) are cited prior work, not rows here.
record.test_reason: The study takes superposition as given (the author says he is 'just assuming superposition to be true') and tests predicted consequences of error correction in computation-in-superposition. It measures activation plateaus and directional sensitivity in GPT2-small. It does not measure feature overlap, capacity allocation, polysemanticity, SAE recoverability or completeness, or feature dimensionality. The author agrees it doesn't distinguish superposition vs no superposition. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author reports plateaus around real GPT2 activations and greater sensitivity to real-other directions, read as consistent with error correction. He admits trivial explanations may exist and that the results don't distinguish superposition from no superposition. A September 2024 edit lowers confidence in the sensitive-direction result because of baseline effects found in Lee & Heimersheim.
record.recipe_differences: Tests residual-stream perturbation effects in GPT2-small rather than the original toy-model setup for superposition; the report does not reproduce the original feature-storage intervention or measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by perturbation direction distribution: isotropic random directions are much less sensitive than covariance-adjusted directions. The real-other versus random sensitivity difference disappears when perturbing at the 12th rather than the 2nd layer. The report tests both straight and sphere perturbation modes.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT2-small, real activations sit on output plateaus under covariance-adjusted random perturbations, unlike random base activations. Perturbations toward other real activations raise KL earlier than random directions, and the real-other direction looks like a local sensitivity optimum in a 2-D interpolation. The author later says baseline effects may largely explain the sensitive-direction result, and the difference vanished when perturbing at layer 12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Error correction / noise suppression in LLM activations: real activations are robust to small random perturbations but sensitive along feature-like directions.

record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: Single model (GPT2-small) and short 10-token openwebtext inputs; results are largely qualitative and plots are not accompanied by tabulated values or uncertainty estimates. The report itself notes plausible alternative explanations and says it does not distinguish superposition from non-superposition explanations. The author later says confidence in the sensitive-direction result is reduced because baseline effects may explain the difference. The local-optimum test explores only two random directions in 768d space.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Cited findings from Gurnee (2024) and Lindsey (2024) were excluded because they are results from other studies.

untested.parts: Toy-model geometry, sparsity-dependent transition and near-orthogonal storage: not examined.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity: not examined.
Non-capacity origins of polysemanticity: not examined.
Whether GPT2 features are distributed across neurons or recoverable by SAEs: not measured. SAE experiments are proposed future work, and SAE sensitivity is cited from Lindsey (2024) only.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units: raised as a concern (dataset illusion) but not tested.
One-dimensional vs multi-dimensional features: not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'assumes': superposition is the premise for the error-correction predictions, not the object of test. The commenter LawrenceC argues the results follow from correct on-distribution behaviour plus linear read-off, without superposition. Interim Alignment Forum report, single model, qualitative plots, no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises through other mechanisms or is evidence of superposition.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons or can be recovered by a dictionary.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.
